title: API & Runtime Gatekeeper: Pluggable Adjudicator for RBAC v2 and Audit Enrichment
creator: Elena Chen
description: Goal: Ship a pluggable adjudicator service + thin middleware for API, runtime, and console that implements RBAC v2 policy evaluation, attaches rich audit events, and supports SSO/SAML identity attributes. Problem: current monolithic authorizer is slow to update, opaque in decisions, and provides poor audit context for incidents and compliance. This work splits evaluation into a small, deterministic adjudicator with a stable API (gRPC/HTTP) and adapters for each surface (API gateway, runtime request path, console backend). The adjudicator will support policy rules, attribute-based checks, time-of-day constraints, and short-lived allow/deny cache. Audit enrichment will add session and SSO assertion metadata (SAML InResponseTo, IdP, assertion attributes) and trace tokens so audit logs are linkable to traces and billing events. Key constraints: <1ms median extra latency for cached checks, tail 99p <15ms for uncached decisions under load, backward compatibility with existing RBAC mappings, no schema changes to customer-facing tokens, and full audit records stored in the existing audit pipeline.
design_notes: Architecture: (1) Adjudicator service implements a compact evaluation engine with a documented policy AST and deterministic semantics. Core engine implemented in Rust for predictable performance; expose a gRPC+HTTP bridge. (2) Middleware adapters: API gateway plugin (Envoy WASM), runtime interceptor (go middleware), console policy client (node). (3) Cache layer: in-process LRU for hot-principal+resource tuples, and a bounded shared cache in redis for cross-pod warmups; cache entries are signed and short-lived (TTL default 30s). (4) Policy language: JSON-DSL with typed attributes, condition operators, and explicit deny precedence. Support for custom extension points via sandboxed WASM checks for enterprise-only logic. (5) Audit enrichment: evaluator returns decision + attributes; adapters enrich audit event with session_id, saml_idp, saml_attrs, principal_ip, token_hash, eval_reason, policy_version, and deterministic decision_id for de-dup. Events emitted to audit-sink topic with schema v2. Performance trade-offs: prefer slightly larger audit payloads for fidelity; provide configurable sampling for verbose policies.
acceptance_criteria: Adjudicator service deployed behind internal LB and reachable from API/runtime/console clients
Middleware adapters implemented and togglable via feature flags for API, runtime, and console
Policy language spec and migration script for existing RBAC rules approved by security
E2E test harness validates identical decisions between legacy authorizer and adjudicator on a 10k rule corpus
Audit events contain required enrichment fields and pass schema validation in audit pipeline
Performance: cached decision p50 <1ms, uncached p99 <15ms at 2000 rps per region in staging
Security review completed and SAML attribute handling documented for privacy
Canary rollout plan executed with automatic rollback on decision divergence >0.1%
